archival_memory.patient_medical_history_2024:
Fasting blood glucose: 135 mg/dL; A1C: 6.9%; Morning readings: 125-130 mg/dL. Action plan: Increase dietary fiber, reduce refined carbs, add light exercise after meals, and monitor daily glucose levels. Weekly routine includes post-meal walks and fiber-rich meals.

Cholesterol results: Total cholesterol: 195 mg/dL(acceptable); LDL: 130 mg/dL(elevated, target: under 100 mg/dL); HDL: 58 mg/dL(excellent); Triglycerides: 140 mg/dL(slightly elevated). Action plan: Increase intake of healthy fats(avocados, nuts, olive oil); reduce saturated fats(red meat, full-fat dairy); maintain current HDL levels; monitor triglycerides regularly.

Blood pressure: 138/85 mmHg(last check-up); target: below 130/80 mmHg. Home readings: 135–140 mmHg(systolic), 80–90 mmHg(diastolic). Factors affecting readings: stress, salt intake. Action plan: Reduce sodium intake, increase water consumption, monitor stress levels, and consider mindfulness or relaxation techniques to support blood pressure control.

Vitamin D: Level: 22 ng/mL(deficient; normal range: 30-50 ng/mL). Action plan: Start 2,000 IU daily supplement; retest in 3-6 months to monitor improvement. Note: Sunlight exposure may be limited due to Kansas weather, especially in winter.

Thyroid: TSH: 2.1 mIU/L(normal range: 0.5-4.5 mIU/L); T4: 1.2 ng/dL(normal). Status: Stable and well-controlled. Levothyroxine dosage is effective. Recommendation: Continue regular monitoring every 6–12 months, especially during seasonal changes or if symptoms shift.

Bone density: Spine T-score: -1.8 (osteopenia); Hip T-score: -1.5 (borderline). Action plan: Increase strength training(e.g., resistance exercises, bodyweight workouts); boost calcium and vitamin D intake; take calcium supplement with vitamin K2 for better absorption. Dietary changes: Add dairy and leafy greens; ensure consistent vitamin D supplementation. Follow-up: Repeat bone density scan in 1–2 years to monitor progression.
archival_memory.diabetes_treatment_plan: Type 2 Diabetes: Metformin 1000 mg twice daily for several years. Recently added semaglutide(Ozempic) at low dose for appetite control and blood sugar management. Fasting blood sugar typically 125-130 mg/dL. A1C around 6.9%.
archival_memory.hypertension_treatment_plan: Losartan 50 mg once daily. Blood pressure typically 135-140/80-90 mmHg. Doctor recommends stress management and reduced sodium intake instead of increasing dosage. Taking a daily magnesium supplement for potential blood pressure support.
archival_memory.hypothyroidism_treatment_plan: Levothyroxine 75 mcg once daily, taken on an empty stomach, 30 minutes before eating. Last TSH test: 2.1 mIU/L(within normal range). No dosage changes needed. Notice sluggishness if a dose is missed; uses a pill organizer to stay on track.
archival_memory.osteoarthritis_treatment_plan: Acetaminophen as needed for mild pain. Meloxicam 7.5 mg prescribed for flare-ups(knees and hands), taken only when joints are stiff, to avoid overuse of NSAIDs. Glucosamine supplements tried, but effect unclear—no definitive improvement noted yet.
archival_memory.vitamin_d_and_bone_health_plan: Vitamin D3 2,000 IU daily due to low levels(22 ng/mL; normal >30 ng/mL). Taking calcium supplements due to early osteopenia on bone density scan. Doctor recommends combining with vitamin K2 to improve calcium absorption and bone health.
archival_memory.cholesterol_management_plan: Atorvastatin 10 mg daily. Initial LDL: 130 mg/dL, triglycerides: 140 mg/dL. Started low-dose statin to improve lipid profile. Cholesterol levels have improved, and no side effects reported(e.g., no muscle aches).
archival_memory.general_health_supplements: Daily multivitamin, omega-3 supplements for heart health, and probiotics for digestion. Post-gallbladder removal: Take digestive enzymes when consuming heavier or fatty meals. Aware that gallbladder removal affects fat digestion, so mindful of dietary fat intake.
archival_memory.medication_interactions_precautions: Aware of potential interactions: NSAIDs(like meloxicam) can affect kidney function when combined with losartan(an ACE inhibitor), so meloxicam is taken only during flare-ups and not frequently. Thyroid medication(levothyroxine) is taken separately from calcium and iron supplements to avoid interference with absorption.
